topic: Standards and specification guidelines for use cases

components.title: The Need for Standardized Use Case Specifications
components.teaches: Students will understand why unstructured product descriptions lead to scope creep and misinterpretation in software projects. They will identify standard use case components necessary for transforming raw ideas into precise functional specifications.

components.title: Defining System Boundaries and Primary vs. Secondary Actors
components.teaches: Students will learn how to construct clear system boundaries that separate internal automated behaviors from external user actions. They will classify primary actors, secondary supporting actors, and external third-party systems from informal text.

components.title: Standard Templates for Brief and Fully Dressed Use Cases
components.teaches: Students will compare standard use case templates, including Cockburn's casual and fully dressed formats. They will learn the mandatory fields required to document a use case brief concisely and unambiguously.

components.title: Extracting Use Cases from Unstructured Narrative Text
components.teaches: Students will apply a step-by-step heuristic to extract actor-goal pairs from informal user feedback and feature requests. They will learn how to filter out UI implementation details while retaining core functional requirements.

components.title: Formulating Main Success Scenarios with Strict Writing Guidelines
components.teaches: Students will learn standard grammatical rules for writing Main Success Scenario steps, such as using subject-verb-object structure, active voice, and explicit actor naming. They will convert informal step descriptions into standardized, sequential action steps.

components.title: Worked Example: Converting a Raw Feature Prompt to Use Case Outlines
components.teaches: Students will watch the step-by-step transformation of a multi-paragraph, messy product description for an e-commerce checkout into formal use case outlines. They will observe how to resolve ambiguous phrases, split compound goals, and establish system boundaries explicitly.

components.title: Specifying Preconditions, Guarantees, and Extension Branches
components.teaches: Students will learn how to formalize entry preconditions, minimal and success guarantees, and exception handling branches in standard use case documentation. They will evaluate trade-offs between detail level and specification maintainability.

components.title: Evaluating Use Case Quality and Completeness Checklist
components.teaches: Students will analyze sample use case outlines against a standard quality checklist to detect boundary leaks, missing actors, and untestable steps. They will discuss how standardized specifications reduce downstream errors in AI-assisted development.
